region: South and North Sulawesi: Toraja highlands, Maros karst, Bira and Minahasa
title: Indonesia — Sulawesi: Cliff Graves, Cave Art and Tarsiers
subtitle: From the Maros karst and Toraja funeral country to the pinisi yards at Bira, then north to tarsier forest and Bunaken
summary: A 15-day Sulawesi route away from Bali and Java: Maros cave art, Toraja highlands and Bira boat yards in the south, Tangkoko forest and Bunaken reef in the north. Conditional on the French piracy wording for the Celebes Sea and the March wet season.
introduction: Sulawesi is the orchid-shaped island east of Borneo, and this route uses its two ends. In the south you take a longboat among tower karst to cave walls painted before farming existed, climb to the Toraja highlands where families still raise carved houses and bury their dead in cliffs, and watch schooners built plank by plank on the beach at Tana Beru. A short flight north brings a cool Minahasa town, a pre-dawn walk to a tarsier's sleeping tree in Tangkoko forest, a strait of black-sand slopes at Lembeh, and the wall reef of Bunaken. Roads are slow, drivers are hired, and March rain shapes every day.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is empty desert with a vehicle, tents and no people for days. Sulawesi is green, wet and crowded with village life: you travel with a hired driver, sleep in guesthouses and homestays, and spend the days among families, markets and boats. The only shared element is the long road.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Package Indonesia sells Bali, Yogyakarta and Komodo. This route has no flights to Bali or Java at all and spends three days in Toraja country with a local guide, one night beside a shipyard, and dawn in a forest reserve with a ranger.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other trip combines some of the world's oldest dated cave art, a living cliff-burial culture and a UNESCO-listed hand shipbuilding tradition with tarsier forest and a coral wall inside one fortnight.

duration.note: Day 1 departure, Day 2 arrival in Makassar, Day 14 departure from Manado, Day 15 arrival in Paris. Thirteen days on the ground.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: March has less rain than February in both Makassar (391 mm against 563 mm) and Manado, and starting after Eid al-Fitr (about 9–10 March) avoids the mass domestic travel days and Ramadan daytime closures in the Muslim-majority parts of South Sulawesi. Easter weekend is 26–28 March and falls after the Toraja days.

februarySuitability.summary: Peak wet season in South Sulawesi: Makassar averages 563 mm and 26 rainy days. Ramadan (about 8 February to 9 March) closes many daytime eateries in Makassar, Pare-Pare and Bira. Mountain roads to Toraja carry landslide risk and the sea off Manado is at its roughest.

marchSuitability.summary: Still wet, but drier than February: Makassar 391 mm and 23 rainy days. The wet season remains a real constraint on Toraja walks, boat trips and photography. Going after Eid (from 13 March) avoids the busiest travel and fasting days.

climate.regionNote: Makassar (1991–2020 normals) for the southern lowlands, Manado (1961–1990) for the north; Toraja highland values are an estimate (cooler by 5–6 C than Makassar, wetter).

february.rainfall: Makassar 563 mm over about 26 days; Manado 361 mm; Toraja highlands estimated at 300 mm or more.
february.notes: Peak wet season in the south.

march.rainfall: Makassar 391 mm over about 23 days; Manado 338 mm; Toraja similar to or slightly below February.
march.notes: Rain usually comes in heavy afternoon bursts with sunny mornings.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: No snow. Toraja mountain roads (Enrekang to Rantepao) can suffer landslides after heavy rain; Batutumonga paths are slippery.
climate.seaConditions: Rough seas are reported on the north coast in December to February; by March the Bunaken and Lembeh crossings are short and sheltered but operators still cancel on windy days. The Bira coast is exposed and dry in March relative to the north.
climate.airQuality: Generally good; forest-fire haze is an April to September issue elsewhere in Indonesia.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Tarsiers and macaques at Tangkoko are present all year. Marine life at Bunaken and Lembeh is year-round; visibility is better April to November.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Affects Muslim-majority South Sulawesi (Makassar, Pare-Pare, Bira) strongly; Toraja and North Sulawesi are Christian-majority and little affected.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Eid al-Fitr (Idul Fitri) and mass travel
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: about 9–10 March 2027, with collective leave days around it
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Flights, buses and hotels are full and expensive around Eid; start the trip on 13 March.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Good Friday and Easter
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Religious processions in Toraja and Minahasa; the route leaves on 27 March.

climate.ramadan2027: Strong impact if travelling in February or before Eid: daytime restaurants closed in the Muslim-majority south. Avoided by travelling from 13 March.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: Chinese-Indonesian celebrations are local and do not affect the route.
climate.tourismDemand: Low season in Toraja and Maros. Few visitors; guides and homestays are easy to find but some tour operators run fewer departures.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Indonesian domestic fares spike around Eid; international fares to Makassar and Manado are moderate in March and are an estimate, not a quote.

geography.summary: A K-shaped island: lowland karst near Makassar, a limestone highland at Toraja, a dry south-east tip, and a volcanic north with forest and coral.
geography.distinctive: Tower karst standing in flooded rice fields with painted caves, highland cliffs that serve as cemeteries, and a wall reef within an hour of a volcanic highland.

landscapes.name: Maros-Pangkep karst
landscapes.description: Tower karst with rivers, rice land and hundreds of caves.

landscapes.name: Toraja highlands
landscapes.description: Terraced valleys and limestone cliffs from 800 to 1,300 m.

landscapes.name: Tangkoko lowland forest
landscapes.description: Forest at the foot of a volcano.

landscapes.name: Bunaken reef wall
landscapes.description: Coral wall dropping into deep water inside a marine park.

culture.summary: Prehistoric cave art in Maros, Toraja funerary culture, Bugis-Makassar seafaring and pinisi building, and Minahasa Christian cuisine and markets.

culturalHighlights.name: Maros-Pangkep cave art
culturalHighlights.description: Hand stencils and animal paintings tens of thousands of years old. Visitors see the open sites at Leang-Leang; the best-known dated panels are reported to be in caves not open to ordinary visitors (not verified).

culturalHighlights.name: Toraja cliff and cave graves
culturalHighlights.description: Lemo, Londa and Kete Kesu: burial cliffs with effigies. Respectful, guided, modest dress, no flash near the dead.

culturalHighlights.name: Toraja funeral ceremonies (Rambu Solo')
culturalHighlights.description: Peak July to October but they also occur in other months. Do not plan around one; if a guide is invited, attend as a quiet guest, dressed in dark clothes, with a small gift.

culturalHighlights.name: Pinisi boat yards at Tana Beru
culturalHighlights.description: UNESCO-listed hand shipbuilding on the beach, where families have built schooners for generations.

culturalHighlights.name: Minahasa market and food
culturalHighlights.description: Tomohon traditional market selling a very wide range of local foods; some items are controversial and nobody has to eat them.

adventureHighlights.name: Batutumonga downhill walk
adventureHighlights.description: 3–4 h guided walk through terraces and villages; slippery in wet weather.

adventureHighlights.name: Tangkoko dawn walk
adventureHighlights.description: Forest walk before sunrise with a ranger to see tarsiers and macaques.

adventureHighlights.name: Bunaken and Lembeh snorkelling
adventureHighlights.description: Snorkelling over a reef wall and a sheltered strait; optional dives for certified divers.

adventureHighlights.name: Rammang-Rammang longboat
adventureHighlights.description: Boat and walk among karst towers.

signatureExperiences.title: Cave art and karst boat ride at Maros
signatureExperiences.description: Longboat up the river at Rammang-Rammang to Kampung Berua and Passaung cave, then the prehistoric hand stencils of Leang-Leang.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Some of the oldest dated rock art in the world is in this karst.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Day trip from Makassar with the driver; local site guide at Leang-Leang. The most famous dated panels are reported to be in caves not open to ordinary visitors; confirm access locally before promising anything.

signatureExperiences.title: Three days in Toraja country
signatureExperiences.description: Kete Kesu, Lemo and Londa burial sites, the market at Rantepao, and a downhill walk from Batutumonga.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A highland culture that keeps its dead among the living and carves them effigies.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local guide for three days; stay in Rantepao homestays. Funerals peak in July to October, so March visits are mostly sites, villages and walks, with a funeral only if one happens to be under way.

signatureExperiences.title: Pinisi shipbuilders at Tana Beru
signatureExperiences.description: Walk the beach yards where wooden schooners are built without plans.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: UNESCO-recognised craft still practised by communities.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Driver from Makassar; ask the yard owners and a Bira guesthouse to introduce you.

signatureExperiences.title: Tarsier dawn at Tangkoko
signatureExperiences.description: Rangers find the spectral tarsiers at their daytime sleeping tree before dawn; the group then follows black macaques.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the smallest primates, watched in primary lowland forest in an area off the main routes.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Overnight in Batuputih and book ranger guides at the park post; no flash, observation distance.

travelStyle.summary: Hired car and driver for all road legs, local guides on site, one domestic flight, short boat trips.

transport.summary: Private car with driver for roads; one flight between Makassar and Manado; short boats. Makassar to Rantepao is 8–9 h by road; the Toraja airport (TRT) is seasonal and was not confirmed for February–March.

modes.description: MPV with driver for the road legs; standard way to travel in Sulawesi.
Makassar to Manado, about 2 h, several daily on full-service and low-cost carriers.
Longboat at Rammang-Rammang, small boats to Lembeh and Bunaken; check life jackets.
Short city rides in Makassar and Manado.

transport.carRental: Self-drive rental exists in Makassar and Manado but is not recommended; a driver is cheaper and safer than the risk on mountain roads. Flights to Toraja (Wings Air) are seasonal and cannot be relied on.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-driving is possible but not advised: left-hand traffic, motorbikes, livestock, landslides and heavy rain. Hire a car with driver.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: A 1949-convention International Driving Permit is required alongside the national licence; FCDO notes a UK licence alone is not valid.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences, but no driving is planned.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody without a motorcycle licence may ride; do not rent scooters. Legal alternatives are riding as a passenger with a hired rider (ojek) where licensed and insured, car with driver, or walking.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Hire a car with driver and local guides.

accommodation.summary: Guesthouses, small hotels and homestays; nights in Pare-Pare and Rantepao can be basic.

camping.summary: Camping is rare and unnecessary: guesthouses are cheap and wet-season camping would be miserable. No nights planned.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Heat, humidity, long drives and one 3–4 h downhill walk. No technical skill.

itinerary.summary: Fly into Makassar, see the Maros karst, drive to Toraja for three days, return to Makassar and Bira for the boat yards, fly north to Manado for Tomohon, Tangkoko, Lembeh and Bunaken, then fly home. Central Sulawesi is deliberately excluded.

days.title: Departure
activities: Fly Paris to Singapore or Kuala Lumpur overnight
days.practical: Check the passport is in good condition: Indonesia turns away damaged passports. Complete the All Indonesia form within 72 h of landing.

days.title: Landing in the old port
activities: Connect to Makassar (about 2 h 45 min from Singapore)
Fort Rotterdam and the La Galigo museum at sunset
days.practical: Buy a local SIM at the airport. Pay the visa on arrival (card or cash).

days.title: Karst, rivers and the oldest paintings
activities: Longboat at Rammang-Rammang to Kampung Berua
Leang-Leang prehistoric park: hand stencils and painted panels open to visitors
days.practical: The best-known dated panels (such as the 45,000-year-old animal painting) are reported to be in caves not open to ordinary visitors; this was not verified with the park authority, so plan for the open Leang-Leang sites only and confirm on the day.

days.title: Up to the highlands
activities: Drive through Enrekang and the mountain road to Toraja
Kete Kesu village in the afternoon
days.accommodation: Rantepao hotel or homestay, 2 twin rooms
days.geographicalHighlight: Mountain road with cloud and landslide risk in the wet months
days.practical: Start before 08:00; rain can slow the road.

days.title: Cliff and cave graves
activities: Londa cave burials with a lamp guide
Ask the local guide whether a funeral is under way and, if invited, go as a quiet guest
days.practical: The Rantepao buffalo market takes place on a six-day cycle; ask your guide.

days.title: Batutumonga and the rice terraces
activities: Guided downhill walk of 3–4 h through terraces to Lokomata and Sandan Uai
days.practical: Contingency day: if rain stops the trek, swap with a village and craft day or an extra funeral visit.

days.title: The long road south
activities: Leave at 06:30; breakfast and lunch stops
days.practical: Long day. A split night in Pare-Pare is possible if the group would rather, at the cost of Bira time.

days.title: Where the schooners are built
activities: Drive to the south-east tip via Bulukumba
Late afternoon walk through the Tana Beru boat yards
days.geographicalHighlight: Sandy bays on a dry coast

days.title: Boat yards, then back
activities: Morning at the yards watching a hull being planked
days.practical: Contingency day: shorten or drop the snorkel if the sea is rough.

days.title: North Sulawesi
days.culturalHighlight: Minahasa food and Christian highland culture
days.practical: Book a flight before midday so a delay still leaves the afternoon.

days.title: Into the forest reserve
activities: Drive across to the Tangkoko edge
days.practical: Bring insect repellent; no wild camping in the reserve.

days.title: Tarsiers at dawn, then the strait
activities: Before dawn: ranger-guided visit to the tarsier sleeping tree (no flash, observation distance)
Drive to Bitung and take a boat for a half-day snorkel along Lembeh
days.transport: Hired car with driver; small boat
days.practical: Boat cancelled on rough days; keep the afternoon flexible.

days.title: Bunaken day
activities: Snorkelling over the reef wall; certified divers can dive
days.practical: Check sea state with the dive operator the evening before.

days.title: Home
activities: Flight Manado to Singapore or Jakarta, then Paris
days.practical: Fly out late in the day so a small delay does not cost the connection.

days.title: Arrival
activities: Land at Paris CDG in the morning

stops.name: Sultan Hasanuddin International Airport (UPG)
stops.description: Arrival airport for Makassar, 30 km north-east of the city centre. International connections arrive from Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Jakarta.
activities: Arrival, SIM card, cash from ATM
stops.transport: Pre-booked driver or Grab (about 45–60 min to the centre).

stops.name: Makassar (Fort Rotterdam and Paotere harbour)
stops.description: Capital of South Sulawesi and the old trading port of the Gowa-Makassar sultanate. Fort Rotterdam houses the La Galigo museum; Paotere harbour still moors wooden Bugis schooners.
activities: Coto Makassar, konro ribs and sea-food at street stalls
stops.culturalImportance: Seat of the Gowa sultanate, Dutch fort from 1670s, home port of Bugis-Makassar sailors.
stops.geography: Flat coastal city on the Makassar Strait.
stops.accommodation: Mid-range city hotel or guesthouse, 2 twin rooms.

stops.name: Rammang-Rammang karst and Leang-Leang caves
stops.description: Tower karst of the Maros-Pangkep area. A longboat goes up the river between karst hills to Kampung Berua; the Leang-Leang prehistoric park, 15 minutes away, has hand stencils and a painted wall that are open to visitors.
activities: Walk to Kampung Berua and Passaung cave
Leang-Leang hand stencils with a local site guide
stops.culturalImportance: Cave art in this karst has been dated to between about 40,000 and 45,000 years; the best-known dated panels are reported to be in caves not open to ordinary visitors (not verified).
stops.geography: Tower karst standing in flooded rice land.
stops.transport: Driver from Makassar, about 1 h to 1.5 h.

stops.name: Pare-Pare
stops.description: Port town on the road to the highlands, used as a break in the long drive to Toraja. Birthplace of a former president; seafood restaurants on the waterfront.
stops.transport: Driver, about 3.5 to 4 h from Maros.

stops.name: Rantepao and Kete Kesu
stops.description: Rantepao is the market town at the centre of Toraja country; Kete Kesu, 4 km away, is a village of boat-roofed tongkonan houses with a cliff of burials behind it.
activities: Local guide for funerals and village visits
stops.culturalImportance: Toraja funeral rituals, ancestral tongkonan houses and carved wood tradition.
stops.geography: Highland valley at about 800 m ringed by green hills.
stops.transport: Driver, about 4 to 5 h from Pare-Pare.
stops.accommodation: Hotel or homestay in Rantepao (2 twin rooms).

stops.name: Lemo cliff graves
stops.description: Cliff face with balconies holding wooden tau-tau effigies, in the valley south of Rantepao.
stops.culturalImportance: Burial place of Toraja nobility; effigies are made once a funeral is complete.
stops.transport: Driver or ojek passenger with a licensed rider.

stops.name: Londa cave burials
stops.description: Cave and cliff cemetery with coffins in the cave mouth. Visited with a lamp-carrying guide.
stops.culturalImportance: Family burial caves still in use.
stops.geography: Limestone cliff with a cave opening.

stops.name: Batutumonga highlands
stops.description: Village on the western flank of Mount Sesean at about 1,300 m, starting point for a 3 to 4 h downhill walk through terraced fields to the villages of Lokomata and Sandan Uai.
stops.geography: Terraced slopes and forest on the Sesean massif.
stops.transport: Driver to the top, walk down, driver at the foot.

stops.name: Tana Beru and Bira (pinisi boat yards)
stops.description: At Tana Beru on the south-east tip of the peninsula, wooden pinisi schooners are built on the beach without plans, as inscribed by UNESCO in 2017. Bira has the nearest white-sand beach.
stops.geography: Dry south coast with sandy bays.
stops.transport: Driver, about 4.5 to 5 h from Makassar.

stops.name: Sam Ratulangi Airport, Manado
stops.description: North Sulawesi airport, about 1 h 45 to 2 h by air from Makassar and with international connections via Singapore or Jakarta.
stops.transport: Flight from Makassar; driver to Tomohon.

stops.name: Tomohon and Lake Linow
stops.description: Highland town of the Minahasa people at about 700 m, with flower nurseries, the traditional market, and the sulphurous Lake Linow. Lokon volcano above the town carries a high alert level and is not climbed.

stops.name: Tangkoko Nature Reserve (Batuputih)
stops.description: Lowland forest reserve with spectral tarsiers and Celebes crested macaques. Visitors enter only from the village of Batuputih.
activities: Dawn tarsier visit at the sleeping tree
stops.geography: Lowland rainforest at the foot of the Tangkoko volcano.
stops.transport: Driver, about 2.5 to 3 h from Tomohon.

stops.name: Lembeh Strait (Bitung)
stops.description: Narrow sheltered strait between Bitung and Lembeh Island known for small marine animals on black-sand slopes. Done as a half-day snorkel by small boat.
stops.transport: Driver from Batuputih, 1 h, then a hired boat.

stops.name: Bunaken Island and marine park
stops.description: Wall reef 30 minutes by boat from Manado. A day of snorkelling over the wall with optional dives, then a return to Manado.
stops.geography: Coral wall dropping to deep water.

security.summary: No official source advises against all or all-but-essential travel for the assessed route. The Netherlands rates all of Indonesia yellow except Papua. France lists piracy in the Celebes, Java and Banda seas under its 'déconseillées sauf raison impérative' heading, which is ambiguous for sheltered tourist boat trips at Bunaken and Lembeh, so the route stays conditional. Central Sulawesi (Poso) is not included, and Lokon volcano is not climbed.
security.assessedRoute: Makassar, Maros, Pare-Pare, Toraja (Rantepao), Bira, Manado, Tomohon, Tangkoko, Bitung/Lembeh, Bunaken. Outside the assessed route: Central Sulawesi (Palu, Poso, Tentena, Togean, Lore Lindu, Bada), Papua.

advisories.level: Papua advised against except imperative reasons; piracy waters (Banda, Java, Celebes seas) under 'zones déconseillées sauf raison impérative'; rest of Indonesia general vigilance
advisories.regionsAffected: Papua; Celebes sea piracy zone; Poso area for terrorism
advisories.routeImpact: Land route is clear; sea trips at Bunaken, Lembeh and Bira are short and coastal, but the wording makes the classification conditional.

advisories.level: No 'advise against' region named; Central Sulawesi flagged as unsettled
advisories.regionsAffected: Central Sulawesi (Palu, Poso, Tentena, Sigi, Parigi Moutong); Papua

advisories.level: Yellow for the rest of Indonesia; orange only for Papua provinces; high volcano alert on Lokon
advisories.routeImpact: Route clear; the Lokon summit is not visited.

conflictRisk.note: No armed conflict in the assessed regions.

terrorismRisk.note: Raised nationwide; groups near Poso (Central Sulawesi) target police. Route avoids Poso.

kidnappingRisk.note: Kidnapping risk named for Papua, not for the route.

regionalRestrictions: Do not enter Central Sulawesi (Poso, Palu, Togean) on this route.
Do not climb Lokon or Mahawu.
Do not plan sea legs beyond coastal day boats.
ordinaryRisks: Road accidents and landslides in the wet season
security.medicalAccess: Private hospitals in Makassar and Manado; serious cases need evacuation to Singapore or France; hospitals ask for insurance guarantees before treating.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Insurance with medical evacuation and cover for snorkelling and boat travel; check that Celebes sea piracy wording does not void cover.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure; triggers include any French or UK warning for Sulawesi, new terrorist incidents in North or South Sulawesi, Lokon eruption, or confirmation of the visa fee.

practicalRequirements.visa: French citizens: 30-day visa on arrival (IDR 500,000 now; increase to 750,000 or 1,000,000 proposed), e-VOA before travel. Other nationalities must check. Bali levy is irrelevant.
practicalRequirements.entry: All Indonesia form within 72 h of arrival; return ticket required.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: More than 6 months and in good condition with blank pages.
permits: Tangkoko ranger guide at the park post
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Good 4G in cities; patchy in Toraja highlands and Tangkoko.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cash rupiah needed in villages; ATMs in Makassar, Rantepao, Manado.
practicalRequirements.medical: Hepatitis A, typhoid, routine vaccines; dengue and malaria precautions; avoid tap water.
